scope_note: Daily edition from matching Wednesday /new listings: 146 non-replacement cs.CV rows, 55 cs.RO rows, 190 deduplicated papers, and 161 ROI papers. Tier A cards use official arXiv abstract pages plus available official arXiv HTML headings.
executive_thesis: The August 5 batch turns world models, SLAM, and VLA execution into one operational question: when should an agent trust, refresh, or discard its internal state? Quo Vadis broadens world models into agent-centric feedback proxies, SLAMFormer-infinity removes a fixed distance bound from SLAM processing, Continue or Replan turns action-chunk horizons into a learned continuation decision, and DRIFT shows flow-matching VLA robustness can fail along the denoising trajectory. APRL's best move is a state-validity benchmark that couples map memory, action horizon, proprioception, and adversarial physical attention.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: World models are feedback interfaces, not only future-video predictors
decision_cards.body: Quo Vadis reframes world proxies around actionable feedback before real actions, matching APRL's need for cheap but typed robot trials.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Long-range SLAM needs flexible memory coordinates
decision_cards.body: SLAMFormer-infinity asks the frontend and backend to process unbounded structure without anchoring everything to the first frame.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Execution horizons and VLA attacks are state-validity problems
decision_cards.body: Continue/Replan and DRIFT both show that hidden trajectory state can become stale or steerable before the final action is emitted.

papers.title: Quo Vadis, World Modeling?
papers.fit: agent-centric world proxies - feedback interface - world-model design space
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML structure checked
papers.status_quo: World models are commonly treated as future physical-state predictors.
papers.friction: Improving agents need feedback that is cheaper and safer than direct real-environment interaction.
papers.hidden_premise: The useful proxy can be any interface that gives actionable feedback before real action, not only a predicted video.
papers.conceptual_move: Shift from physical-state prediction to agent-centric world proxies and their functional forms.
papers.mechanism: The official HTML headings lay out motivation, definition, empowerment, instantiations, and design-space conclusion.

evidence.claim: The paper says world models offer lower-cost, controllable feedback before real actions.
Official HTML includes Definition and Instantiations sections for agent-centric world proxies.
APRL should classify WAMs by feedback type: image, state, critic, planner, or monitor.

papers.falsification: If proxy feedback does not predict real-world action improvement, the broadened design space becomes taxonomy without leverage.
papers.adversarial: A broad proxy definition can hide weak grounding unless every proxy is tied to a success and stop condition.
papers.thinking_tool: Before building a world model, name the feedback channel and the real action it is supposed to change.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for robot learning and agent evaluation; less direct for pure generative-media tasks.

papers.title: SLAMFormer-infinity: Infinite SLAM Transformer for Unbounded Frontend and Backend Processing
papers.fit: SLAM transformer - unbounded memory - frontend/backend geometry
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML structure checked
papers.status_quo: Transformer SLAM often has a bounded context or first-frame-anchored coordinate formulation.
papers.friction: Long-range frontend and backend processing need flexible coordinate systems and memory conditions.
papers.hidden_premise: The SLAM memory coordinate should be redefined as the sequence grows rather than fixed at frame one.
papers.conceptual_move: Use memory conditions to define flexible coordinate systems and scales for unbounded processing.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes memory-conditioned frontend and backend processing without an explicit distance bound.

evidence.claim: The paper claims support for long-range frontend and backend processing without an explicit distance bound.
Official HTML includes Methodology and Experiments sections.
APRL's map benchmark should measure when memory coordinates become stale or inconsistent.

papers.falsification: If unbounded processing fails under loop closure, dynamic objects, or calibration drift, the memory condition is not enough.
papers.adversarial: Transformer context can appear unbounded while computation or map update cost still grows operationally.
papers.thinking_tool: Evaluate SLAM memory by coordinate validity and update cost, not just endpoint trajectory error.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for visual SLAM and localization; less direct for sparse LiDAR-only systems.

papers.title: Continue or Replan? Bernoulli-Continuation Policy Learning for Adaptive Horizon Execution
papers.fit: VLA execution horizon - replanning boundary - adaptive control
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML structure checked
papers.status_quo: Chunk-based VLA policies often execute a fixed number of actions before replanning.
papers.friction: A critical manipulation stage can be executed from a stale chunk if no replanning boundary arrives in time.
papers.hidden_premise: The policy should learn whether its current chunk remains valid.
papers.conceptual_move: Add a Bernoulli continuation decision that adaptively decides continue versus replan.
papers.mechanism: The official abstract positions BCP as a lightweight plug-and-play adaptive horizon framework.

evidence.claim: The paper names fixed execution horizons as task-agnostic periodic schedules.
Official HTML includes Method and Experiments sections.
APRL should ablate chunk age, continuation probability, and failure onset together.

papers.falsification: If adaptive replanning only increases compute without improving critical-stage success, the continuation signal is weak.
papers.adversarial: A continuation head can learn dataset rhythm rather than true task progress.
papers.thinking_tool: Treat replanning as a learned validity test for the current action chunk.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for chunk-based manipulation; less relevant for continuous MPC controllers.

papers.title: DRIFT: Derailing Denoising Trajectories of Flow-Matching VLAs with Adversarial Patch Attack
papers.fit: flow-matching VLA security - denoising trajectory - physical attention hijacking
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML structure checked
papers.status_quo: Flow-matching VLAs have been reported to resist attacks that fool autoregressive VLAs.
papers.friction: Prior attacks can ignore the multi-step denoising ODE where action trajectories are formed.
papers.hidden_premise: Robustness must be tested along the denoising path, not only at the final output.
papers.conceptual_move: Attack the denoising trajectory with a universal adversarial patch on the robot's scene.
papers.mechanism: The official abstract says DRIFT redirects the flow-matching trajectory through test-time input perturbation.

evidence.claim: The paper says apparent robustness stems from attacks ignoring the multi-step denoising ODE.
Official HTML includes Methodology and Experiments sections.
APRL should monitor intermediate denoising states for attack or drift evidence.

papers.falsification: If trajectory attacks fail under real camera lighting, viewpoint, and object clutter, physical transfer is limited.
papers.adversarial: Patch attacks can overstate risk if they require unrealistic placement or visibility.
papers.thinking_tool: Audit generative policies at every internal refinement step, not only at the emitted action.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for flow-matching VLA policies; less direct for discrete action decoders.

synthesis.title: State validity ties world models, maps, and action chunks
synthesis.facts: The papers each replace a fixed state assumption: physical future only, first-frame coordinate, fixed action horizon.
synthesis.inference: APRL should evaluate when internal state is valid enough to act and when it must be refreshed.

synthesis.title: Robustness must be checked before the final decision
synthesis.links: DRIFT - proprioceptive VLA state - visual evidence scheduling
synthesis.facts: The batch has attacks, proprioception, token pruning, and evidence-scheduling papers.
synthesis.inference: Intermediate state audits are a better moat than another end-to-end success comparison.

strategy.title: State-validity benchmark for robot agents
strategy.thesis: Couple map memory, action chunk age, proprioceptive history, and attack trajectory into one validity benchmark.
strategy.one_week: Instrument one VLA rollout with chunk age, replan decision, proprioception window, map age, and denoising-step drift.
strategy.four_week: Build a small suite where stale map, stale chunk, missing proprioception, and adversarial patch are crossed.
strategy.success: The benchmark predicts failure family before final action failure in at least two stress conditions.
strategy.stop: State validity signals do not separate failure families beyond generic confidence.
strategy.asset: Robot-agent state-validity logs plus replayable stress scenarios.
